food.title: Food manufacture
food.question: What is inventory flexibility worth?
food.intro: Change the monthly holding charge and vegetable refining capacity. Compare the six-month production and inventory plan with the original case.
food.assumptions: Five oils, six months, 150 GBP/t selling price. Nonvegetable capacity is 250 t/month. Each oil starts and ends at 500 t. Holding is charged on all six closing stocks, including June.

equations.label: Inventory balance
equations.math: previous stock + purchases = processing + closing stock
equations.why: Purchases can be shifted between months, but mass cannot disappear. Each oil has its own balance.

equations.label: Profit
equations.why: A lower holding charge changes the objective coefficients. It does not create new refining capacity.

food.challenge: Find a case with lower holding charges but unchanged total production. Explain where the profit improvement comes from.

blend.title: Robust blending
blend.question: How much protection will you buy?
blend.intro: Increase the uncertainty budget or tighten the quality specification. Watch the least-cost recipe change and distinguish protected quality from a full-box stress test.
blend.assumptions: 100 t/day of product; each feed is limited to 60 t/day. Costs are 100, 80, and 55 USD/t. Nominal impurity is 2%, 8%, and 14%; upward deviations are 1, 2, and 3 percentage points. Γ is an uncertainty-set budget, not a probability.

equations.label: Mass balance
equations.why: A cheap feed can only replace another feed; it cannot change the production target.

equations.label: Robust quality
equations.math: nominal impurity load + worst permitted deviation ≤ limit × 100
equations.why: The worst permitted deviation is calculated over the selected uncertainty budget. Full-box protection requires Γ = 3.

blend.challenge: At a 7% limit, compare Γ = 0, 1.5, and 3. Explain why the intermediate recipe can pass its protected check but fail the full-box stress test.

hydrogen.title: Hydrogen storage
hydrogen.question: Store hydrogen or buy expensive power?
hydrogen.intro: Choose a tank size and change electricity prices during periods 3 and 4. Compare total daily cost, including the same capacity charge for every tank.
hydrogen.assumptions: Six four-hour periods; power ≤ 4 MW; 0.05 MWh/kg; initial and final stock 50 kg. Capacity costs 0.15 USD/(kg day). Production and withdrawal are uniform within each period. No startup charges or minimum load in this experiment.

equations.label: Hydrogen balance
equations.math: end stock = previous stock + 4 × power / 0.05 − demand
equations.why: Power is in MW. Multiply by four hours before converting electricity to kilograms.

equations.label: Daily cost
equations.why: Every comparison includes ownership cost. A larger tank can move production in time without reducing daily energy use.

hydrogen.challenge: At the original prices, find the best tank in the selectable menu. Explain why increasing capacity beyond that point can raise total cost.
